title: [AUG-108] Use first-written-byte time as system capture start for track alignment
why_we_need_this:
Follow-up to AUG-105. systemOffsetMs is computed as capture.startedAt minus the client's micStartedAt, where startedAt is the moment the server spawned ffmpeg (@server/src/services/systemCapture.ts). Device startup latency between spawn and the first audio sample (typically 100 to 300 ms, more for a cold audiotee tap) is not compensated, so the system track is systematically stamped earlier than it really started. The acceptance target is 500 ms; the current approach probably fits but with little margin and no measurement.

Design:
1. After spawn, poll the output WAV file size (fs.stat every 25 ms, max 2 s) and record firstByteAt when the size first exceeds the 44-byte header. Use firstByteAt as the capture startedAt returned by /start and stored on the capture; fall back to spawn time if the poll times out.
2. Expose both spawnedAt and startedAt in the /start and /stop responses for debugging.
3. Write the applied systemOffsetMs into the transcript header rendered by renderTranscript (e.g. "- Track offset: +182 ms") so a user who sees misordered lines can report the number.
4. Add a Praxis note (not code) in the architecture README that cross-correlation of the two tracks is the next step if real transcripts still show misordering.
acceptance_criteria:
- POST /api/capture/start returns startedAt equal to the first-written-byte time, and spawnedAt separately; startedAt minus spawnedAt is logged at debug level.
- If no bytes are written within 2 s, startedAt falls back to spawnedAt and the response includes startedAtSource: 'spawn'.
- Dual-track transcripts produced from a server capture include a "Track offset" line in the header; browser dual recordings and single uploads do not.
- A unit test covers the offset header rendering for offset 0 (omitted), positive, and negative values.
- Existing alignDualSegments tests still pass; no change to mergeDualStream.
important_constraints:
- Do not change the client micStartedAt contract; only the server side of the offset moves.
- Polling must stop as soon as the first byte is seen; do not leave an interval running for the capture lifetime.
